name: Metal Servants: A Century of Robots
description: From the film Metropolis and Elektro to Unimate, Roomba, Atlas and the Mars rovers: how robots moved from imagination to factories, homes and other planets.

checkpoints.name: Imagined machines
checkpoints.note: The film Metropolis gave the screen a famous robot in 1927. Elektro, a tall walking showpiece built by Westinghouse, appeared at the 1939 New York World's Fair and showed the public what a robot might look like.

checkpoints.name: Factories and labs
checkpoints.note: Unimate went to work on a car factory line in 1961, the first industrial robot. Shakey could reason about its surroundings, Lunokhod 1 roamed the Moon, and 2001 and Star Wars filled cinemas with machines.

checkpoints.name: Play and rivals
checkpoints.note: Blade Runner asked what separates people from machines. Tamagotchi made a digital pet a toy, and Deep Blue beat the chess champion in 1997 showing software could now outplay people.

checkpoints.name: Robots come home
checkpoints.note: AIBO was a robot dog, and Honda's ASIMO walked on two legs. The da Vinci Surgical System helped surgeons, the Roomba vacuumed floors, and the Mars Exploration Rovers drove on another planet.

checkpoints.name: Smarter machines
checkpoints.note: Curiosity and Perseverance explored Mars, Baxter worked beside factory staff, and Atlas learned to run and jump. Pepper and Sophia tried to talk with people, while AlphaGo won at the board game Go.
